title: Three purchase events
fullTitle: One Click. Three Purchase Events. Here’s What Went Wrong.

scenes.narration: One completed order, transaction T dash zero zero zero one. And in the local collector, three purchase envelopes for it. Same event name, same transaction ID, three different senders.
captions: One completed order. Three received purchase envelopes.
Same event, same transaction ID, three senders.

scenes.narration: Rewind to the click. The customer confirmed once. The order completed once. Then the confirmation screen appeared. That is one business event.
captions: Rewind: one click, one completed order, one confirmation screen.

scenes.narration: But three pieces of code were listening. The app's purchase handler. A tag-manager trigger on the same event bus. And the confirmation component, which fires purchase every time it mounts. Each sent its own envelope.
captions: Three emitters: app handler, tag-manager trigger, component mount.
Each sent its own envelope to the collector.

scenes.narration: Inspect them. Event name: purchase, three times. Transaction ID: identical. Emitter: three different sources. Timestamps seven and fourteen milliseconds apart. Not three orders. Three claims on one order.
captions: emitter: three sources · ts: milliseconds apart

scenes.narration: The problem: several components each believe they own the same business event. A caution, though. Three raw envelopes are not three GA4 conversions. GA4 documents deduplicating purchase by matching transaction ID on web streams. That covers purchase, not every event, and it hides duplication rather than fixing it.
captions: Several components claim ownership of one business event.
3 raw envelopes ≠ 3 GA4 conversions. GA4 documents purchase dedup by transaction_id (web).
That covers purchase, not every event. It hides duplication; it does not fix it.

scenes.narration: Choose one authoritative path. The purchase handler runs when the order actually completes, so it owns the event.
captions: One authoritative emitter: the handler that runs when the order completes.

scenes.narration: Remove the tag-manager purchase trigger. Delete the emission from the component's mount handler. The component still renders; it simply no longer reports.
captions: Remove the tag-manager trigger. Remove the mount-handler emission.
The component still renders. It no longer reports.

scenes.narration: Repeat the action. Complete the same order, then remount the confirmation component, twice.
captions: Retest: complete the same order, then remount the component twice.

scenes.narration: Received count: one. One envelope, from the purchase handler, same transaction ID. In this tested scenario only. This is not exactly-once delivery across reloads, retries or devices; replaying the same order is a separate idempotency problem.
captions: Tested scenario only. Not exactly-once across reloads, retries or devices.
Order-level idempotency is a separate design concern.

scenes.narration: Fix the emitters. Then verify the reporting.
captions: Fix the emitters. Then verify the reporting.
